messages:
elaine: Hey team — Acme trial is wrapping today. Need a quick ops checklist for tearing down the POC env: revoke hosted API keys, remove dedicated pool p-acme-01, and confirm data retention/export. Legal asked to preserve message logs for 45 days. Can we coordinate?

mike: I can handle the hosted keys and pool deletion. Do we have the final list of key IDs and pool id?

jon: Pushing the list here — keys: key_live_akj32, key_test_b9c11. Pool id: p-acme-01. Also: they used a VPC peering for private deployment; docs say we should remove peering after handoff.

nina: legal hold: we only need 45 days of logs for this customer, then permanent delete. Please export queryable logs to the secure bucket before deletion. Bucket: gs://redwood-poc-exports/acme-1728 (access restricted).

ash: Ack. Plan: 1) snapshot KV/cache and export logs to the bucket; 2) rotate/invalidate Hosted keys; 3) deallocate dedicated pool; 4) remove VPC peering and firewall rules; 5) purge any ephemeral S3/FS mounts after 45 days.

elaine: @mike @ash can we do steps 1–3 today? Customer wants confirmation that they no longer have access to any keys by EOD.

mike: I'll rotate the hosted keys now. Commands I will run:
```bash
# invalidate hosted keys
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/key_live_akj32/invalidate -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/key_test_b9c11/invalidate -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
# deprovision dedicated pool (force if idle)
redwoodctl pools delete --id p-acme-01 --force
```
I'll post back the operation IDs.

ash: I'll start the export snapshot. Quick note: snapshot size ~12GB, ETA ~6m. I'll trigger export to gs://redwood-poc-exports/acme-1728/export-172863.

sre-bot: [deploy-bot] export job created: export-172863, status: queued.

mike: Invalidate calls done. Responses: 200 OK (key_live_akj32), 200 OK (key_test_b9c11). Operation IDs: op_9981, op_9982.

jon: Confirmed — their app immediately started getting 401s, good. Customer noted they removed local copies too.

ash: Export finished: export-172863 -> gs://redwood-poc-exports/acme-1728/export-172863.tar.gz (sha256: abcd1234). Starting pool delete now.

mike: Pool delete returned 202 accepted, job pdel-77a. Will watch until terminated.

nina: When pool is gone, please remove the VPC peering on both sides. Leave a final audit entry in the case file: acme-poc-closure-172863. Legal will verify retention.

ash: VPC peering removal scheduled. Command I'm running:
```bash
# remove peering from our side
cloudctl network peerings delete --project redwood-prod --peering acme-peer-1728
# confirm route cleanup
cloudctl network routes list --filter "acme-peer-1728"
```
I'll annotate the audit log with the export sha and operation IDs.

sre-bot: [pool-service] p-acme-01 termination complete (pdel-77a).

mike: Pool confirmed terminated. All runtime nodes shut down.

elaine: Thanks everyone. Nina, legal will you confirm retention policy satisfied on your end?

nina: Confirmed. We'll keep the exported archive for 45 days in the restricted bucket and then trigger secure deletion. Please tag the export object with: retention=45d, case=acme-poc-closure-172863.

ash: Tagged and set lifecycle rule to auto-delete after 46 days (slight buffer). Also removed firewall rules referencing the VPC subnet.

jon: From Acme: "Thanks — confirmed we no longer have access and appreciate the clean handoff."

elaine: I'll close the sales POC in CRM and attach the audit notes. Final checklist status: keys invalidated, export archived, pool torn down, VPC peering removed, retention set. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:

mike: FYI — I pushed a tiny doc in #docs with the quick teardown commands under /playbooks/poc-cleanup.md

ash: Added the audit ids to case file: op_9981, op_9982, pdel-77a, export-172863.

sre-bot: [audit] case acme-poc-closure-172863 closed by elaine at 1728633600

elaine: Great work, team. :tada:
